source.text: וַתִּשָּׂא֙ כָּל־הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה וַֽיִּתְּנ֖וּ אֶת־קוֹלָ֑ם וַיִּבְכּ֥וּ הָעָ֖ם בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הַהֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And lifted up all the congregation and gave their voice, and wept the people in the night the that.

en.L: And all the congregation lifted up and gave forth their voice, and the people wept on that night.
en.B: Then the whole congregation raised a loud cry, and the people wept that night.
en.R: That night the whole community cried out loudly, and the people wept.

es.L: Y toda la comunidad alzó y dio su voz, y el pueblo lloró aquella noche.
es.B: Entonces toda la comunidad prorrumpió en grandes gritos, y el pueblo lloró aquella noche.
es.R: Aquella noche toda la comunidad gritó con fuerza, y la gente lloró.

fr.L: Et toute la communauté éleva et fit entendre sa voix, et le peuple pleura cette nuit-là.
fr.B: Alors toute la communauté poussa de grands cris, et le peuple pleura cette nuit-là.
fr.R: Cette nuit-là, toute la communauté a crié très fort, et le peuple a pleuré.

sw.L: Kisha jumuiya yote ikainua, ikatoa sauti yake, nao watu wakalia usiku ule.
sw.B: Ndipo jumuiya yote ikapaza kilio kikubwa, na watu wakalia usiku ule.
sw.R: Usiku ule jumuiya nzima ilipiga kelele kwa sauti kubwa, na watu wakalia.

decisions.choice: lifted up and gave forth their voice: cried out aloud
decisions.reason: The first verb, "lift up", has no object; it is completed by the second phrase, "gave their voice". Together they describe a loud outcry of grief and protest, which turns into weeping. The report of the spies in 13:31-33 is the cause.

decisions.choice: congregation: the whole people of Israel gathered as one community
decisions.reason: The word names Israel as an assembled body (1:2; Exodus 12:3). The chapter uses it for the whole people who now turn against the LORD's plan, and the LORD calls them "this evil congregation" (verses 27, 35).

decisions.choice: lifted up and gave forth their voice
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two verbs and does not supply an object for the first, so the reader sees that "their voice" serves both. Balanced and Readable join them into one phrase about a loud cry.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("éleva", "pleura"); passé composé at Readable ("a crié", "a pleuré")
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the Pentateuch: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative, the passé composé the tense of spoken French that new readers know. Speech keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

source.text: וַיִּלֹּ֨נוּ֙ עַל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְעַֽל־אַהֲרֹ֔ן כֹּ֖ל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֲלֵהֶ֜ם כָּל־הָעֵדָ֗ה לוּ־מַ֨תְנוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם א֛וֹ בַּמִּדְבָּ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה לוּ־מָֽתְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And grumbled against Moses and against Aaron all [the] sons of Israel, and said to them all the congregation, if only we had died in [the] land of Egypt, or in the wilderness the this, if only we had died.

en.L: And all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel grumbled against Moses and against Aaron, and all the congregation said to them, "If only we had died in the land of Egypt, or in this wilderness, if only we had died!
en.B: All the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, "We wish we had died in the land of Egypt, or else died here in this wilderness!
en.R: All the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} complained about Moses and Aaron. The whole community said to them, "We wish we had died in Egypt! We wish we had died here in the desert!

es.L: Y murmuraron contra Moisés y contra Aarón todos los hijos de Israel, y les dijo toda la comunidad: «¡Ojalá hubiéramos muerto en la tierra de Egipto, o en este desierto, ojalá hubiéramos muerto!
es.B: Todos los israelitas murmuraron contra Moisés y Aarón, y toda la comunidad les dijo: «¡Cómo quisiéramos haber muerto en la tierra de Egipto, o aun aquí, en este desierto!
es.R: Todos los israelitas se quejaron de Moisés y Aarón. Toda la comunidad les dijo: «¡Ojalá hubiéramos muerto en Egipto! ¡Ojalá hubiéramos muerto aquí en el desierto!

fr.L: Et tous les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël murmurèrent contre Moïse et contre Aaron, et toute la communauté leur dit : « Si seulement nous étions morts dans le pays d’Égypte, ou dans ce désert, si seulement nous étions morts !
fr.B: Tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} murmurèrent contre Moïse et Aaron, et toute la communauté leur dit : « Nous aurions préféré mourir dans le pays d’Égypte, ou même mourir ici, dans ce désert !
fr.R: Tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} se sont plaints de Moïse et d’Aaron. Toute la communauté leur a dit : « Si seulement nous étions morts en Égypte ! Si seulement nous étions morts ici, dans le désert !

sw.L: Na wana wote wa Israeli wakanung'unika juu ya Musa na juu ya Haruni, na jumuiya yote ikawaambia, "Laiti tungalikufa katika nchi ya Misri, au katika nyika hii, laiti tungalikufa!
sw.B: Waisraeli wote waliwanung'unikia Musa na Haruni, na jumuiya yote ikawaambia, "Afadhali tungekufa katika nchi ya Misri, au hata tungekufa hapa katika nyika hii!
sw.R: Waisraeli wote walilalamika juu ya Musa na Haruni. Jumuiya nzima ikawaambia, "Heri tungalikufa huko Misri! Heri tungalikufa hapa jangwani!

decisions.choice: grumbled: complained in bitter protest
decisions.reason: The verb is used for Israel's complaints in the wilderness (Exodus 15:24; 16:2, 7-8; 17:3). It is more than unhappiness: it is protest that turns against Moses and Aaron and, as Exodus 16:8 says, against the LORD himself. The LORD takes it up in verses 27 and 29.

decisions.choice: if only we had died: a wish about the past
decisions.reason: The small word that opens each half of the cry expresses a wish that cannot come true. The wish is said twice, at the start and at the end, for force.

decisions.choice: died in this wilderness: the wish the LORD will grant
decisions.reason: In verses 28-29 the LORD answers the people with their own words: "As you have spoken in my hearing, so I will do to you: in this wilderness your corpses will fall." Their wish becomes their sentence.

decisions.choice: We wish we had died
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "we wish" for the Hebrew wish word, which reads naturally in a cry of complaint. Literal keeps "if only" at both ends of the sentence, as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: "Nous aurions préféré mourir"
decisions.reason: Balanced says the wish as a regret in modern French, as the English Balanced does with "we wish"; Literal and Readable keep "si seulement" at both ends of the cry. "Que ne sommes-nous morts" is too old-fashioned for a public reading today.

source.text: וְלָמָ֣ה יְ֠הוָה מֵבִ֨יא אֹתָ֜נוּ אֶל־הָאָ֤רֶץ הַזֹּאת֙ לִנְפֹּ֣ל בַּחֶ֔רֶב נָשֵׁ֥ינוּ וְטַפֵּ֖נוּ יִהְי֣וּ לָבַ֑ז הֲל֧וֹא ט֦וֹב לָ֖נוּ שׁ֥וּב מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And why [is] Yahweh bringing us to the land the this to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will become plunder. [Is it] not good for us to return to Egypt?

en.L: And why [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bringing us into this land, to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will become plunder. [Would it] not [be] better for us to return to Egypt?"
en.B: What is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} doing, bringing us into this land just so we can be killed in battle? Our wives and little ones will be carried off as spoil. Would going back to Egypt not be better for us?"
en.R: Why is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} taking us to this land? We will be killed in battle, and enemies will capture our wives and children. It would be better for us to go back to Egypt!"

es.L: ¿Y por qué nos trae {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a esta tierra, para caer a espada? Nuestras mujeres y nuestros pequeños serán botín. ¿No [sería] mejor para nosotros volver a Egipto?».
es.B: ¿Qué está haciendo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, trayéndonos a esta tierra solo para que muramos en la batalla? Nuestras mujeres y nuestros niños pequeños serán llevados como botín. ¿No sería mejor que volviéramos a Egipto?».
es.R: ¿Por qué nos lleva {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a esa tierra? Allí nos matarán en la guerra, y los enemigos se llevarán a nuestras mujeres y a nuestros hijos. ¡Sería mejor volver a Egipto!».

fr.L: Et pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous amène-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dans ce pays, pour tomber par l’épée ? Nos femmes et nos petits deviendront un butin. Ne [serait-il] pas mieux pour nous de retourner en Égypte ? »
fr.B: Que fait donc {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} en nous amenant dans ce pays, sinon nous faire tuer au combat ? Nos femmes et nos petits enfants seront emmenés comme butin. Ne vaudrait-il pas mieux pour nous retourner en Égypte ? »
fr.R: Pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous emmène-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dans ce pays ? Nous allons être tués à la guerre, et les ennemis vont prendre nos femmes et nos enfants. Il vaudrait mieux retourner en Égypte ! »

sw.L: Na kwa nini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anatuleta katika nchi hii, tuanguke kwa upanga? Wake zetu na watoto wetu wadogo watakuwa nyara. Je, si [ingekuwa] vema kwetu kurudi Misri?"
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anafanya nini, akituleta katika nchi hii ili tu tuuawe vitani? Wake zetu na watoto wetu wadogo watachukuliwa kama nyara. Je, si afadhali turudi Misri?"
sw.R: Kwa nini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anatupeleka katika nchi hiyo? Tutauawa vitani, na adui watawachukua wake zetu na watoto wetu. Ni afadhali turudi Misri!"

decisions.choice: to fall by the sword: to be killed in battle
decisions.reason: "Fall by the sword" means to die at the hands of an enemy army. The people believe the report that the towns are strong and the people are giants (13:28, 31-33).

decisions.choice: little ones: young children
decisions.reason: The word means children too young to march or fight, who would be taken with the women as captives when a people was defeated (Deuteronomy 20:14). In verse 31 the LORD promises that these same little ones will enter the land.

decisions.choice: is it not better: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question is a way of stating firmly that going back would be better. The word "good" here, comparing two choices, means "better".

decisions.choice: What is the LORD doing
decisions.reason: The Hebrew asks "why" of what the LORD is doing, as a complaint more than a request for a reason. Balanced makes the protest plain; Literal and Readable keep "why".

decisions.choice: enemies will capture
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the wives and children "will become plunder"; Readable names who would take them, the enemies the people fear.

decisions.choice: It would be better for us to go back to Egypt!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question that expects "yes" into the statement it makes.

decisions.choice: "nous amène-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}"
alternatives: no deity_pronoun span, as in the English
decisions.reason: A French question with a noun subject repeats it as an inverted pronoun, so French has a pronoun for the LORD where the English has none; it takes the deity_pronoun span like every other pronoun for God.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־אָחִ֑יו נִתְּנָ֥ה רֹ֖אשׁ וְנָשׁ֥וּבָה מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said each to his brother, let us appoint a head, and let us return to Egypt.

en.L: And they said each one to his brother, "Let us appoint a head and let us return to Egypt."
en.B: And they said to one another, "Let us put someone at our head and go back to Egypt."
en.R: They said to each other, "Let us choose a new leader and go back to Egypt."

es.L: Y dijeron cada uno a su hermano: «Pongamos un jefe y volvamos a Egipto».
es.B: Y se decían unos a otros: «Pongámonos un jefe y volvamos a Egipto».
es.R: Se dijeron unos a otros: «Elijamos un nuevo líder y regresemos a Egipto».

fr.L: Et ils dirent chacun à son frère : « Établissons un chef, et retournons en Égypte. »
fr.B: Et ils se dirent les uns aux autres : « Mettons quelqu’un à notre tête et retournons en Égypte. »
fr.R: Ils se sont dit entre eux : « Choisissons un nouveau chef et retournons en Égypte. »

sw.L: Wakasema kila mtu kwa ndugu yake, "Tumweke mkuu, na turudi Misri."
sw.B: Wakaambiana, "Tumchague mtu atuongoze, turudi Misri."
sw.R: Wakaambiana, "Tumchague kiongozi mpya, turudi Misri."

decisions.choice: each to his brother: to one another
decisions.reason: "A man to his brother" is the usual Hebrew way of saying "to one another"; it does not mean only family members.

decisions.choice: appoint a head and return: a rejection of Moses and of the LORD who brought them out
decisions.reason: Choosing a new head means setting Moses aside, and going back to Egypt means undoing the exodus. Nehemiah 9:17 remembers this moment: "they appointed a head to return to their slavery".

decisions.choice: a new leader
decisions.reason: Readable adds "new" to show that the leader they want would replace Moses, which is what choosing a head means here.

source.text: וַיִּפֹּ֥ל מֹשֶׁ֛ה וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן עַל־פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם לִפְנֵ֕י כָּל־קְהַ֥ל עֲדַ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And fell Moses and Aaron on their faces before all [the] assembly of [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: Then Moses and Aaron fell face down in front of the whole assembly of the congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: Then Moses and Aaron threw themselves face down on the ground in front of all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who were gathered there.

es.L: Y cayeron Moisés y Aarón sobre sus rostros delante de toda la asamblea de la comunidad de los hijos de Israel.
es.B: Entonces Moisés y Aarón se postraron rostro en tierra delante de toda la asamblea de la comunidad de los israelitas.
es.R: Entonces Moisés y Aarón se echaron al suelo boca abajo delante de todos los israelitas que estaban allí reunidos.

fr.L: Et Moïse et Aaron tombèrent sur leur face devant toute l’assemblée de la communauté des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël.
fr.B: Alors Moïse et Aaron se jetèrent face contre terre devant toute l’assemblée de la communauté des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}.
fr.R: Alors Moïse et Aaron se sont jetés à plat ventre par terre devant tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} qui étaient rassemblés là.

sw.L: Ndipo Musa na Haruni wakaanguka kwa nyuso zao mbele ya kusanyiko lote la jumuiya ya wana wa Israeli.
sw.B: Ndipo Musa na Haruni walianguka kifudifudi mbele ya kusanyiko lote la jumuiya ya Waisraeli.
sw.R: Ndipo Musa na Haruni wakajitupa chini kifudifudi mbele ya Waisraeli wote waliokuwa wamekusanyika pale.

decisions.choice: fell on their faces: lay face down in distress and appeal
decisions.reason: To fall on one's face is a gesture of deep humility, fear or pleading. Moses and Aaron do it again when the people rebel (16:4, 22; 20:6). Here it shows their dismay and their turning to God, before the whole people.

decisions.choice: the assembly of the congregation: the whole people gathered in one place
decisions.reason: Two words for Israel as a gathered people stand together for emphasis: everyone was there to see.

decisions.choice: all the Israelites who were gathered there
decisions.reason: Readable puts the two words for the gathered people into one plain phrase.

source.text: וִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־נ֗וּן וְכָלֵב֙ בֶּן־יְפֻנֶּ֔ה מִן־הַתָּרִ֖ים אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ קָרְע֖וּ בִּגְדֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, from those spying out the land, tore their clothes.

en.L: And Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, from those who spied out the land, tore their clothes.
en.B: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, two of the men who had explored the land, tore their clothes.
en.R: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh had been among the men who explored the land. They tore their clothes to show their grief.

es.L: Y Josué hijo de Nun y Caleb hijo de Jefone, de los que habían explorado la tierra, rasgaron sus vestidos.
es.B: Josué hijo de Nun y Caleb hijo de Jefone, dos de los hombres que habían explorado la tierra, rasgaron su ropa.
es.R: Josué hijo de Nun y Caleb hijo de Jefone habían estado entre los hombres que exploraron la tierra. Rasgaron su ropa en señal de dolor.

fr.L: Et Josué fils de Noun et Caleb fils de Jephounné, d’entre ceux qui avaient exploré le pays, déchirèrent leurs vêtements.
fr.B: Josué fils de Noun et Caleb fils de Jephounné, deux des hommes qui avaient parcouru le pays, déchirèrent leurs vêtements.
fr.R: Josué, fils de Noun, et Caleb, fils de Jephounné, faisaient partie des hommes qui avaient exploré le pays. Ils ont déchiré leurs vêtements pour montrer leur douleur.

sw.L: Na Yoshua mwana wa Nuni na Kalebu mwana wa Yefune, wa wale walioipeleleza nchi, wakararua nguo zao.
sw.B: Yoshua mwana wa Nuni na Kalebu mwana wa Yefune, wawili kati ya watu walioipeleleza nchi, walirarua nguo zao.
sw.R: Yoshua mwana wa Nuni na Kalebu mwana wa Yefune walikuwa miongoni mwa watu walioipeleleza nchi. Walirarua nguo zao kuonyesha huzuni yao.

decisions.choice: tore their clothes: a sign of grief and horror
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes was the usual sign of mourning or of shock at a terrible event (Genesis 37:29, 34; 2 Kings 18:37). Joshua and Caleb are appalled at what the people are saying.

decisions.choice: spied out: explored and scouted
decisions.reason: The verb means to go about and search out a land, as the twelve men were sent to do (13:2, 16-17). The same verb returns in verses 7, 34, 36 and 38.

decisions.choice: two of the men who had explored
decisions.reason: "From those who spied out" means they were among the twelve. Balanced says "two of the men" to make that clear.

decisions.choice: to show their grief
decisions.reason: Readable says what tearing one's clothes meant.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֶל־כָּל־עֲדַ֥ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבַ֤רְנוּ בָהּ֙ לָת֣וּר אֹתָ֔הּ טוֹבָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ מְאֹ֥ד מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel, saying, the land which we passed through it to spy it out, good [is] the land very very.

en.L: And they said to all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, saying, "The land which we passed through to spy it out, the land [is] very, very good.
en.B: They said to the whole congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, "The land we traveled through to explore is a good land, very good indeed.
en.R: They told the whole community, "We went through that land and explored it. It is a very, very good land.

es.L: Y hablaron a toda la comunidad de los hijos de Israel, diciendo: «La tierra por la que pasamos para explorarla, la tierra [es] muy, muy buena.
es.B: Y dijeron a toda la comunidad de los israelitas: «La tierra que recorrimos para explorarla es una tierra buena, realmente muy buena.
es.R: Le dijeron a toda la comunidad: «Recorrimos esa tierra y la exploramos. Es una tierra muy, muy buena.

fr.L: Et ils parlèrent à toute la communauté des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, en disant : « Le pays que nous avons parcouru pour l’explorer, le pays [est] très, très bon.
fr.B: Ils dirent à toute la communauté des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} : « Le pays que nous avons parcouru pour l’explorer est un bon pays, un pays vraiment excellent.
fr.R: Ils ont dit à toute la communauté : « Nous avons traversé ce pays et nous l’avons exploré. C’est un pays très, très bon.

sw.L: Wakaiambia jumuiya yote ya wana wa Israeli, wakisema, "Nchi tuliyopita ndani yake ili kuipeleleza, nchi hiyo [ni] njema sana sana.
sw.B: Waliiambia jumuiya yote ya Waisraeli, "Nchi tuliyoipitia kuipeleleza ni nchi nzuri, nzuri kupita kiasi.
sw.R: Waliiambia jumuiya nzima, "Tuliipitia nchi ile na kuipeleleza. Ni nchi nzuri sana sana.

decisions.choice: very, very good: an exceptionally good land
decisions.reason: The word "very" is doubled for strong emphasis. Joshua and Caleb answer the other spies, who said the land "eats up its inhabitants" (13:32), and the people's fear in verse 3. The land's goodness echoes God's promise of a good land (Exodus 3:8).

decisions.choice: a good land, very good indeed
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the doubled "very" as an added phrase of emphasis rather than repeating the word.

source.text: אִם־חָפֵ֥ץ בָּ֨נוּ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וְהֵבִ֤יא אֹתָ֨נוּ֙ אֶל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וּנְתָנָ֖הּ לָ֑נוּ אֶ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־הִ֛וא זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: If delights in us Yahweh, and he will bring us into the land the this and give it to us, a land which it [is] flowing [with] milk and honey.

en.L: If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} delights in us, then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land which flows [with] milk and honey.
en.B: If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} takes delight in us, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land where milk and honey flow.
en.R: If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is pleased with us, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lead us into this land and give it to us. It is a rich land, flowing with milk and honey.

es.L: Si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se complace en nosotros, nos llevará a esta tierra y nos la dará, una tierra que fluye leche y miel.
es.B: Si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se agrada de nosotros, nos hará entrar en esta tierra y nos la dará: una tierra que fluye leche y miel.
es.R: Si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está contento con nosotros, nos llevará a esa tierra y nos la dará. Es una tierra rica, que fluye leche y miel.

fr.L: Si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} prend plaisir en nous, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous fera entrer dans ce pays et nous le donnera, un pays où coulent le lait et le miel.
fr.B: Si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous est favorable, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous conduira dans ce pays et nous le donnera, un pays où coulent le lait et le miel.
fr.R: Si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est content de nous, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous fera entrer dans ce pays et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous le donnera. C’est un pays riche, où coulent le lait et le miel.

sw.L: Ikiwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anapendezwa nasi, atatuingiza katika nchi hii, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atatupa, nchi itiririkayo maziwa na asali.

decisions.choice: delights in us: is pleased with us and favors us
decisions.reason: The verb means to take pleasure in someone and choose to do them good. Joshua and Caleb do not doubt God's power; what matters is the people's relationship with him. Verse 9 says how they could lose his favor: by rebelling.

decisions.choice: flowing with milk and honey: a rich and fertile land
decisions.reason: This is the LORD's own description of the land since he first promised it to Moses (Exodus 3:8, 17). Milk points to good pasture for flocks and herds, and honey to sweet food, from bees or from fruit such as dates. The spies had used the same words (13:27).

decisions.choice: It is a rich land
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and adds "rich" to say what the picture means, while keeping the picture.

en.L: Only do not rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and you, do not fear the people of the land, for they [are] our bread. Their shade has turned away from over them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] with us. Do not fear them."
en.B: Just do not rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And as for you, have no fear of the people who live in the land; we will eat them up like bread. The shelter over them has been taken away, while {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with us. So do not fear them!"
en.R: But do not turn against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And do not be afraid of the people who live there. We will swallow them up as easily as bread. Nothing protects them anymore, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with us. Do not be afraid of them!"

Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo de la gente que vive en esa tierra; nos los comeremos como pan. fr.B: Seulement, ne vous rebellez pas contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Et vous, n’ayez pas peur des habitants du pays : nous les dévorerons comme du pain. L’abri qui les couvrait leur a été retiré, alors que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est avec nous. N’ayez donc pas peur d’eux ! »
fr.R: Mais ne vous tournez pas contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Et n’ayez pas peur des gens qui habitent là-bas. Nous les avalerons aussi facilement qu’un morceau de pain. Plus rien ne les protège, mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est avec nous. N’ayez pas peur d’eux ! »

decisions.choice: rebel: rise up against one's rightful lord
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a subject or vassal who revolts against his king (Genesis 14:4; 2 Kings 18:7). Refusing to go into the land the LORD is giving would be rebellion against Israel's King, not only fear.

decisions.choice: they are our bread: we will devour them easily
decisions.reason: To be someone's bread is to be eaten up by them, overcome without trouble (compare 24:8 and Psalm 14:4). It answers the spies' claim that the land "eats up its inhabitants" (13:32): it is the enemies who will be eaten.

decisions.choice: their shade has turned away from them: their protection is gone
decisions.reason: In a hot land, shade is shelter and safety, and the word is often used for protection, including God's (Psalm 91:1; 121:5; Isaiah 30:2-3). Whatever defended the people of the land, whether their strength or their gods, has left them.

decisions.choice: we will eat them up like bread / swallow them up as easily as bread
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "they are our bread" into a plain statement and keep the picture of bread, so the answer to 13:32 is still heard.

decisions.choice: The shelter over them
decisions.reason: "Shade" alone could sound like a picture of darkness in English. Balanced says "shelter", which keeps the sense of protection overhead.

decisions.choice: "tutawameza" (we will swallow them)
decisions.reason: "We will eat them" is "tutawala" in Swahili, which reads first as "we will rule". "Tutawameza" keeps the picture of eating with bread and cannot be misread. Literal keeps "mkate wetu" (our bread).

decisions.choice: said to stone them: proposed to stone them
decisions.reason: "Said to" with a verb means they spoke of doing it, called for it. They were about to act when God intervened. "Them" are most naturally Joshua and Caleb, who had just spoken; Moses and Aaron may be included too.

decisions.choice: the glory of the LORD appeared: God shows his presence to step in
decisions.reason: The glory of the LORD was the visible sign of his presence, a brightness in the cloud over the tent (Exodus 16:10; 40:34-35). In Numbers it appears when the people rebel, to stop them and to bring judgment (16:19; 17:7; 20:6).

decisions.choice: where all the Israelites could see it
decisions.reason: The glory appeared "to" all Israel. Readable says that it was in plain sight of the whole people.

decisions.choice: despise: treat with contempt, spurn
decisions.reason: The verb means to reject someone with scorn, to treat them as worthless. It returns in verse 23 ("those who despised me") and in 16:30. Refusing God's gift is treating God himself with contempt.

decisions.choice: believe in me: trust me, rely on me
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold firm to someone and rely on them. It is the trust Israel showed after the crossing of the sea (Exodus 14:31) and that Abram showed in God's promise (Genesis 15:6). Here the people refuse to rely on God to keep his word about the land.

decisions.choice: the signs I have done among them: the plagues and the wonders of the wilderness
decisions.reason: The signs are the wonders in Egypt (Exodus 10:1-2) and the LORD's care since: the sea, the manna, the water from the rock (Exodus 14-17). Verse 22 names them again.

decisions.choice: scorn (Balanced); show no respect for (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "despise". Balanced uses "scorn" and Readable a plain phrase for the same contempt.

decisions.choice: I have done so many miracles among them!
decisions.reason: Readable makes the last phrase a sentence of its own and uses "miracles", the plain word for the signs.

decisions.choice: pestilence: a deadly epidemic disease
decisions.reason: The word names a deadly plague, one of the judgments of God (Exodus 5:3; 9:3, 15). It is a different word from the "plague" of verse 37.

decisions.choice: dispossess: cut them off from their inheritance
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for driving the nations out of the land so that Israel can possess it (Exodus 34:24; Numbers 33:52-53). The LORD threatens to do to Israel what he will do to the Canaanites: take away their place and their future in the land.

decisions.choice: I will make you a nation greater than they: the offer God made after the golden calf
decisions.reason: After the golden calf, God told Moses, "I will make of you a great nation" (Exodus 32:10), as he had promised Abraham (Genesis 12:2). As there, Moses does not accept, but pleads for the people (verses 13-19; Exodus 32:11-14).

decisions.choice: them / they (for "it")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the people as "it", one body. Balanced and Readable say "them" and "they", as English does for a people.

decisions.choice: take away their inheritance (Balanced); remove them from their place (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Dispossess" here does not mean driving them out of a land they live in, since they have none yet. Balanced and Readable say what is threatened: the loss of what was promised to them.

decisions.choice: "nitawapiga ... kuwanyang'anya" (them), not a singular "it"
alternatives: "nitalipiga taifa hili" (I will strike this nation)
decisions.reason: Swahili has no neutral "it" for a people; the singular would need a class 5 noun such as "taifa" that the Hebrew does not have here. Literal uses the plural agreement of "watu hawa" (verse 11), as Balanced and Readable in English do.

decisions.choice: then Egypt will hear: what would follow if God destroyed Israel
decisions.reason: Moses answers the threat of verse 12 by saying what it would lead to. "Egypt" stands for the Egyptians. Verses 13-16 are one long thought: Egypt will hear, will tell the people of Canaan, and the nations will say that the LORD failed.

decisions.choice: you brought up this people by your power: God's reputation is bound up with Israel
decisions.reason: The exodus was done so that Egypt would know that he is the LORD (Exodus 7:5; 14:4, 18). Moses argues as he did after the golden calf (Exodus 32:12): if God destroys his people now, the Egyptians will misread what he did.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the Egyptians", since the country stands for its people. Literal keeps "Egypt".

decisions.choice: ends with a comma
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 14, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma. Readable ends the sentence here and starts again in verse 14.

source.text: וְאָמְר֗וּ אֶל־יוֹשֵׁב֮ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּאת֒ שָֽׁמְעוּ֙ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה בְּקֶ֖רֶב הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־עַ֨יִן בְּעַ֜יִן נִרְאָ֣ה׀אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה וַעֲנָֽנְךָ֙ עֹמֵ֣ד עֲלֵהֶ֔ם וּבְעַמֻּ֣ד עָנָ֗ן אַתָּ֨ה הֹלֵ֤ךְ לִפְנֵיהֶם֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וּבְעַמּ֥וּד אֵ֖שׁ לָֽיְלָה׃

en.L: and they will say [it] to the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [are] in the midst of this people, that eye to eye {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, are seen, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} cloud stands over them, and in a pillar of cloud {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go before them by day, and in a pillar of fire by night.
en.B: and they will tell it to those who live in this land. These have heard that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, are present among this people; that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} to them openly, eye to eye; that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} cloud rests above them; and that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} lead the way before them, in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night.
en.R: They will tell the people who live in this land. Those people have already heard that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, are with Israel. They know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} let {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} be seen face to face, that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} cloud stays over {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, and that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go ahead of them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire at night.

fr.R: Ils vont le raconter aux gens qui habitent ce pays. Ces gens savent déjà que {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es avec Israël. Ils savent que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} laisses voir face à face, que {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nuée reste au-dessus de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple, et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} marches devant eux dans une colonne de nuée le jour et dans une colonne de feu la nuit.

decisions.choice: they will say to the inhabitants of this land; they have heard: the news will reach people who already know of God's presence
alternatives: the Egyptians have heard that you are among this people
they will say to the inhabitants of this land that they have heard ...
decisions.reason: The connection of the two clauses is loose in the Hebrew. Most likely the Egyptians will tell the people of Canaan, who have themselves heard what the LORD does for Israel (compare Exodus 15:14-16; Joshua 2:9-11). It may also be the Egyptians who "have heard", or the clause may say what they will tell. In each reading the point is the same: the nations know that the LORD is with this people.

decisions.choice: eye to eye you are seen: you show yourself openly, close at hand
decisions.reason: "Eye to eye" means directly and plainly, face to face (Isaiah 52:8). It describes how near and visible the LORD's presence is to Israel, in the cloud and fire, and in the way he speaks with Moses (12:8; Exodus 33:11).

decisions.choice: your cloud ... a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night
decisions.reason: The cloud stood over the tabernacle and led Israel on its journeys (9:15-23; 10:34), and the pillar of cloud and fire went before them from the start (Exodus 13:21-22).

decisions.choice: show yourself to them openly, eye to eye
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the Hebrew picture and adds "openly" to say what it means. Readable uses the English idiom "face to face".

decisions.choice: with Israel; over your people
decisions.reason: Readable names the people rather than repeating "this people".

decisions.choice: "toi, SEIGNEUR" with the divine_name span on "SEIGNEUR|Yahvé" alone
decisions.reason: The name stands in apposition to "you", as an address; French drops the article in address, so the span carries the name without "le", and both options ("toi, SEIGNEUR", "toi, Yahvé") read naturally.

source.text: וְהֵמַתָּ֛ה אֶת־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה כְּאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֑ד וְאָֽמְרוּ֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־שָׁמְע֥וּ אֶֽת־שִׁמְעֲךָ֖ לֵאמֹֽר׃

sw.R: Kama utawaua watu hawa wote kwa wakati mmoja, mataifa yaliyosikia habari {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} yatasema,

decisions.choice: as one man: all together, at a single stroke
decisions.reason: "As one man" means all at once, as if the whole people were a single person struck down (Judges 20:1, 8 use it of a people acting together).

decisions.choice: and you will put to death: a condition, if you kill
decisions.reason: The verb form joined by "and" sets out a case: if God did what verse 12 says, this is what would follow. Verse 16 gives what the nations would say.

decisions.choice: your fame: the report about you
decisions.reason: The word means what is heard about someone, his reputation. The nations have heard about the LORD's deeds (Exodus 15:14; Joshua 9:9).

decisions.choice: [if]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets out the condition with a verb form alone; Literal supplies "if" in brackets, and Balanced and Readable simply say "if".

source.text: מִבִּלְתִּ֞י יְכֹ֣לֶת יְהוָ֗ה לְהָבִיא֙ אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אֶל־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־נִשְׁבַּ֣ע לָהֶ֑ם וַיִּשְׁחָטֵ֖ם בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Because not able [was] Yahweh to bring the people the this into the land which he swore to them, and he slaughtered them in the wilderness.

en.L: 'Because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was not able to bring this people into the land which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} slaughtered them in the wilderness.'
en.B: 'It was because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was unable to bring this people into the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had sworn to give them that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} butchered them in the wilderness.'
en.R: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was not strong enough to bring these people into the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised them. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} killed them out in the desert.'

es.L: “Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no pudo llevar a este pueblo a la tierra que les había jurado, los degolló en el desierto”.
es.B: “Como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no fue capaz de llevar a este pueblo a la tierra que les había jurado dar, los masacró en el desierto”.
es.R: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no tuvo fuerza suficiente para llevar a esta gente a la tierra que les prometió. Por eso los mató en el desierto”.

fr.L: “Parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} n’était pas capable de faire entrer ce peuple dans le pays qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur avait juré, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a égorgés dans le désert.”
fr.B: “C’est parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était incapable de faire entrer ce peuple dans le pays qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait juré de leur donner qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a massacrés dans le désert.”
fr.R: “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} n’était pas assez fort pour faire entrer ces gens dans le pays qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur avait promis. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a tués dans le désert.”

sw.L: 'Kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakuweza kuwaingiza watu hawa katika nchi aliyowaapia, amewachinja nyikani.'
sw.B: 'Ni kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alishindwa kuwaingiza watu hawa katika nchi aliyoapa kuwapa, ndiyo maana amewachinja nyikani.'
sw.R: '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakuwa na nguvu za kutosha kuwaingiza watu hawa katika nchi aliyowaahidi. Kwa hiyo aliwaua huko jangwani.'

decisions.choice: because the LORD was not able: the nations would think God powerless
decisions.reason: Moses' argument is that the nations would not see judgment but failure: a God who could bring Israel out of Egypt but could not bring them in. Deuteronomy 9:28 repeats it.

decisions.choice: the land which he swore to them: the land he promised them on oath
decisions.reason: God swore to give the land to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and their descendants (Genesis 26:3; Exodus 13:5; 32:13). "To them" here means to this people, as the heirs of that oath; verse 23 says "to their fathers".

decisions.choice: slaughtered: killed like animals
decisions.reason: The verb is used of killing animals for food or sacrifice, and so of killing people without mercy. It is how the nations would describe what God had done.

decisions.choice: had sworn to give them
decisions.reason: Balanced says "to give", which the oath about the land implies.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה יִגְדַּל־נָ֖א כֹּ֣חַ אֲדֹנָ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ לֵאמֹֽר׃

en.R: So now, Lord, please show how great {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power is. You said:

fr.R: Alors maintenant, Seigneur, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie, montre combien {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} puissance est grande. Tu as dit :

sw.L: Na sasa, tafadhali, nguvu za Bwana wangu na ziwe kuu, kama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ulivyosema, ukisema,

sw.R: Basi sasa, Bwana, tafadhali onyesha jinsi nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} zilivyo kuu. Ulisema,

decisions.choice: my Lord: a title of respect for God
decisions.reason: This is not the divine name but the title "Lord", "my master", used in respectful address (Exodus 4:10; 34:9). Moses speaks of God in the third person, as a servant addresses his master.

decisions.choice: let the power of my Lord be great: let God's strength be shown in forgiving
decisions.reason: Moses asks God to show his power, which the nations would doubt (verse 16), not by destroying the people but by keeping his word about his own character, which Moses quotes next (verse 18). Power here is the power to forgive and still bring the people in.

decisions.choice: be shown to be great
decisions.reason: God's power cannot grow; the request is that it be seen to be great. Balanced adds "shown".

decisions.choice: Lord, please show how great your power is
decisions.reason: Readable turns Moses' respectful third person ("the power of my Lord") into direct address, which is how the request reads in plain English.

source.text: יְהוָ֗ה אֶ֤רֶךְ אַפַּ֨יִם֙ וְרַב־חֶ֔סֶד נֹשֵׂ֥א עָוֺ֖ן וָפָ֑שַׁע וְנַקֵּה֙ לֹ֣א יְנַקֶּ֔ה פֹּקֵ֞ד עֲוֺ֤ן אָבוֹת֙ עַל־בָּנִ֔ים עַל־שִׁלֵּשִׁ֖ים וְעַל־רִבֵּעִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh [is] long of anger(s) and great of steadfast love, lifting iniquity and transgression, and leaving unpunished not he leaves unpunished, visiting [the] iniquity of fathers on sons, on third-generation and on fourth-generation.

en.L: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] long of anger and great of steadfast love, bearing iniquity and transgression; but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will by no means acquit [the guilty], visiting the iniquity of fathers on {{gender:children|sons}}, on the third and on the fourth [generation].'
en.B: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is slow to grow angry and rich in faithful love, forgiving wrongdoing and rebellion. Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will never acquit the guilty; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings the wrongdoing of {{gender:parents|fathers}} upon their {{gender:children|sons}}, to the third and the fourth generation.'
en.R: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is slow to become angry, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love is great. He forgives wrongdoing and rebellion. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not let the guilty go free. He deals with the sin of {{gender:parents|fathers}} in the lives of their {{gender:children|sons}}, even as far as the third and fourth generation.'

es.L: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [es] lento para la ira y grande en amor fiel, que carga con la iniquidad y la rebelión; pero de ningún modo absuelve [al culpable], visitando la iniquidad de los padres sobre los hijos, sobre la tercera y sobre la cuarta [generación]”.
es.B: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es lento para enojarse y rico en amor fiel; perdona la maldad y la rebelión. Pero nunca declara inocente al culpable; hace recaer la maldad de los padres sobre sus hijos, hasta la tercera y la cuarta generación”.
es.R: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no se enoja fácilmente, y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor fiel es grande. Perdona el mal y la rebelión. Pero no deja que el culpable quede libre. Pide cuentas del pecado de los padres en la vida de sus hijos, hasta la tercera y aun la cuarta generación”.

fr.L: “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [est] lent à la colère et grand en amour fidèle, qui lève la faute et la transgression ; mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne tient nullement [le coupable] pour innocent, visitant la faute des pères sur les {{gender:enfants|fils}}, sur la troisième et sur la quatrième [génération].”
fr.B: “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est lent à se mettre en colère et riche en amour fidèle ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pardonne la faute et la rébellion. decisions.choice: Moses quotes the LORD's own words to him at Sinai (Exodus 34:6-7)
decisions.reason: "As you have spoken" (verse 17) points to the time the LORD passed before Moses and proclaimed his name (Exodus 34:6-7). Moses repeats the heart of it, in a shorter form: he leaves out "compassionate and gracious", "and faithfulness", "keeping steadfast love to thousands" and the third word for sin, and keeps God's patience, his steadfast love, his forgiveness, and his justice. He asks God to act now as he said he is. That proclamation followed the golden calf, when God also forgave a rebellious people (Exodus 32-34).

decisions.choice: long of anger: slow to become angry, patient
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:6: anger is pictured as a nose or nostrils that are "long", slow to burn hot. It means patient and slow to punish.

decisions.choice: great of steadfast love: abounding in loyal, faithful love
decisions.reason: The word means kindness and love that stay loyal to a relationship and do not give up, the love of the LORD's covenant with Israel (Exodus 20:6; 34:6). Verse 19 builds the plea on its "greatness".

decisions.choice: bearing iniquity and transgression: forgiving wrongdoing and rebellion
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift and carry; with sin as its object it means to carry it away, to forgive (Exodus 34:7; Psalm 32:1, 5). Iniquity is crooked wrong and the guilt it brings; transgression is rebellion, breaking faith. The same verb returns in verse 19 ("as you have forgiven") and in verses 33-34, where the people will "bear" their own wrong.

decisions.choice: he will by no means acquit: he will certainly not treat the guilty as innocent
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis, as in Exodus 34:7: "acquitting, he will not acquit". Its object, the guilty, is understood. Forgiveness does not mean that wrong is treated as though it were never done, which is what happens in verses 20-23: the people are spared, but the guilty generation will not enter the land.

decisions.choice: visiting the iniquity of fathers on children: the effects of sin reach later generations
decisions.reason: To "visit" is to attend to, here to bring the consequences of wrongdoing (Exodus 20:5; 34:7). In this chapter the children of the rebels will share forty years in the wilderness because of their parents (verse 33), and yet will enter the land (verse 31). Each person answers for his own sin (Deuteronomy 24:16; Ezekiel 18:20).

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:6, Balanced and Readable say "faithful love" and Literal "steadfast love". Both keep the loyalty in the word, which "love" alone would lose.

decisions.choice: will never acquit the guilty (Balanced); will not let the guilty go free (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:7, Balanced and Readable name "the guilty" without brackets and render the doubled verb with "never" or a plain "not".

decisions.choice: deals with the sin of parents in the lives of
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:7, Readable says in plain words what "visiting iniquity on" means.

decisions.choice: "lento para la ira" (L), "lento para enojarse" (B), "no se enoja fácilmente" (R); "grande en amor fiel" (L), "rico en amor fiel" (B)
decisions.reason: The words Moses quotes from Exodus 34:6 are worded the same way wherever the formula returns in the Old Testament. "Amor fiel" is the settled term for steadfast love; "misericordia" would be the word for mercy, and "tardo" is archaic.

decisions.choice: "los padres", "los hijos" with no gender span
alternatives: gender spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Spanish "padres" already means parents and "hijos" already includes daughters, so the one wording serves both English options.

decisions.choice: "mkawivu wa hasira" (L), "huchelewa kukasirika" (B), "hakasiriki upesi" (R); "upendo usiokoma" for steadfast love
decisions.reason: Fresh wording for the formula of Exodus 34:6, used wherever it returns. "Si mwepesi wa hasira, mwingi wa fadhili" is the wording of a copyrighted Swahili Bible; "upendo usiokoma" is the settled term.

decisions.choice: "qui lève la faute" (L); "ne tient nullement [le coupable] pour innocent" (L), "ne déclare jamais innocent le coupable" (B), "ne laisse pas le coupable impuni" (R)
decisions.reason: Moses quotes Exodus 34:6-7, and the French uses the same wording as there. "Porter la faute" would suggest bearing the punishment rather than carrying the wrong away (m4); Balanced and Readable say "pardonne". The doubled verb (m5) is carried by "nullement" and "jamais".

decisions.choice: "hamhesabu kamwe [mwenye hatia] kuwa hana hatia" (L); "hamtangazi kamwe mwenye hatia kuwa hana hatia" (B)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:7, which Moses quotes: the doubled verb (m5) means God will never treat or declare the guilty innocent, and "kamwe" carries the emphasis. Readable says "hamwachi mwenye hatia aende huru", as there.

decisions.choice: pardon: forgive, the forgiveness that only God gives
decisions.reason: This verb for forgiving is used in the Old Testament only with God as the one who forgives (Exodus 34:9; Leviticus 4:20). The LORD answers with the same verb in verse 20.

decisions.choice: as you have forgiven: literally "lifted" or "borne"
decisions.reason: This is the verb of verse 18, "bearing iniquity". Moses asks God to go on doing what he has done since the exodus, at the sea, with the manna, after the golden calf (Exodus 32:14; 34:9-10).

decisions.choice: according to the greatness of your steadfast love: the measure and ground of the request
decisions.reason: Moses does not appeal to anything in the people but to the size of God's own love, which he has just named (verse 18).

decisions.choice: pardon ... forgiven
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced use "pardon" for the first verb and "forgive" for the second, so the two Hebrew verbs are kept apart. Readable says "forgive" for both.

decisions.choice: "perdonar" for both verbs
decisions.reason: The English keeps "pardon" and "forgive" apart at Literal and Balanced. Spanish has no second everyday verb for forgiving: "absolver" would echo the "absuelve" of verse 18, which renders a different Hebrew verb (acquit), and "soportar" says only "put up with". The meaning decisions say which Hebrew verb is which.

decisions.choice: "Pardonne" ... "tu as fait grâce à"
decisions.reason: As the English does with "pardon" and "forgive", Literal and Balanced keep the two Hebrew verbs apart; Readable says "pardonner" for both.

decisions.choice: "samehe" ... "umewachukulia" (you have borne with them)
decisions.reason: "Kuchukulia" is the second Hebrew verb's picture of carrying, and in Swahili it means to bear with and forgive someone; it keeps the two verbs apart as the English does. Readable says "kusamehe" for both.

decisions.choice: I have pardoned: God will not destroy the people, as he had threatened
decisions.reason: God grants Moses' prayer: he will not strike the people down at once (verse 12). The pardon does not cancel every consequence, as verse 18 said: the generation that refused the land will not enter it (verses 21-23). The pattern follows Exodus 32:14, 34.

decisions.choice: pardoned them, as you asked
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "them", the people Moses prayed for, and say "as you asked" for "according to your word".

decisions.choice: as I live: a solemn oath
decisions.reason: People swore "as the LORD lives"; God, having no one greater to swear by, swears by his own life (verse 28; Deuteronomy 32:40; Isaiah 49:18). What follows is certain.

decisions.choice: and as all the earth will be filled with the glory of the LORD: part of the oath
alternatives: as I live, all the earth will be filled with the glory of the LORD
decisions.reason: The clause can be read as a second thing God swears by, as sure as his own life: his glory will fill the earth. It can also be read as the first thing he swears to: "as I live, all the earth will be filled with my glory". Either way, his glory will be known everywhere, the very thing Moses feared would be lost (verses 13-16), even though this generation will not enter the land.

decisions.choice: the glory of the LORD filling the earth
decisions.reason: The same hope is sung in Psalm 72:19 and promised in Isaiah 6:3 and Habakkuk 2:14.

decisions.choice: ends with a comma
decisions.reason: The oath runs on through verses 22-23, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma. Readable closes the oath formula with a colon and gives what is sworn in the next verses.

decisions.choice: I make this promise
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that this is an oath.

en.R: All these men saw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory. They saw the miracles I did in Egypt and in the desert. Yet they have tested {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} these ten times, and they have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: tested me: put God to the proof, demanded that he show himself again
decisions.reason: To test God is to doubt him and demand proof that he is with them, as at Massah (Exodus 17:2, 7; Psalm 95:8-9). After all they had seen, they still refused to trust him.

decisions.choice: these ten times: again and again
decisions.reason: "Ten times" may be a round number for many times, as in Genesis 31:7. It may also count the people's acts of testing since leaving Egypt, at the sea, at Marah, with the manna and the water, the golden calf, and in Numbers 11-14.

decisions.choice: the men: the generation that rejected the land
decisions.reason: The men meant are those counted in the census, twenty years old and upward (verse 29). The sentence that begins here finds its verb in verse 23.

decisions.choice: listened to my voice: obeyed
decisions.reason: To "listen to the voice" of someone is to obey them (Exodus 19:5).

decisions.choice: ends with a comma

decisions.choice: surely they will not see: the content of the oath
decisions.reason: In an oath the word "if" stands for a strong "not": "if they see" means "may it be so if they see", that is, they will certainly not see. God swore to give the land to their fathers (Genesis 50:24; Exodus 33:1); now he swears that this generation will not enter it.

decisions.choice: those who despised me: the same word as verse 11
decisions.reason: The verb is the "despise" of verse 11. Their refusal of the land was contempt for the LORD who gave it.

decisions.choice: swore to give their fathers / promised their ancestors with an oath
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "to give" or "promised", which the oath about the land means.

decisions.choice: scorned (Balanced); treated with contempt (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

records.literal_gloss: But my servant Caleb, because was a spirit other with him and he filled after me, and I will bring him into the land where he went to there, and his offspring will possess it.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave Caleb, because there was another spirit with him and he fully followed after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I will bring him into the land where he went, and his offspring will take possession of it.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Caleb is different: there is another spirit in him, and he has followed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all his heart. So I will bring him into the land that he entered, and his descendants will take possession of it.
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Caleb has a different attitude. He has followed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all his heart. So I will bring him into the land he explored, and his descendants will own it.

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} esclavo Caleb, porque hubo otro espíritu con él y fue en pos de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} plenamente, lo llevaré a la tierra adonde fue, y su descendencia la poseerá.
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Caleb es distinto: hay en él otro espíritu, y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha seguido de todo corazón. Por eso lo llevaré a la tierra en la que entró, y sus descendientes la poseerán.
es.R: Pero {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Caleb tiene una actitud diferente. Me ha seguido de todo corazón. Por eso lo llevaré a la tierra que exploró, y sus descendientes serán sus dueños.

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esclave Caleb, parce qu’il y a eu un autre esprit avec lui et qu’il a pleinement marché après {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je le ferai entrer dans le pays où il est allé, et sa descendance en prendra possession.
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Caleb est différent : il y a en lui un autre esprit, et il {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a suivi de tout son cœur. Je le ferai donc entrer dans le pays où il est allé, et ses descendants en prendront possession.
fr.R: Mais {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Caleb a une autre attitude. Il {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a suivi de tout son cœur. Alors je le ferai entrer dans le pays qu’il a exploré, et ses descendants le posséderont.

sw.L: Lakini mtumwa {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Kalebu, kwa sababu kulikuwa na roho nyingine pamoja naye, naye amenifuata kikamilifu, nitamwingiza katika nchi aliyoiendea, na uzao wake utaimiliki.
sw.B: Lakini mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Kalebu ni tofauti: ana roho nyingine ndani yake, naye amenifuata kwa moyo wake wote. Kwa hiyo nitamwingiza katika nchi aliyoiingia, na wazao wake wataimiliki.

decisions.choice: my servant: one who belongs to the LORD and serves him
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a slave, a person owned by a master, not hired. Said by God, "my servant" is a title of honor for one who belongs to him and does his will, as Moses is called (12:7-8; Exodus 14:31).

decisions.choice: another spirit was with him: a different attitude and outlook
decisions.reason: "Spirit" here means a person's inner disposition, the attitude that moves him (Genesis 41:8; Ezekiel 11:19). Caleb's trust in God made him unlike the others, who spread fear (13:30-33).

decisions.choice: he filled after me: he followed me fully
decisions.reason: "To fill after" someone is to follow them completely, holding nothing back. The phrase is used of Caleb and Joshua again and again (32:11-12; Deuteronomy 1:36; Joshua 14:8-9, 14).

decisions.choice: I will bring him into the land where he went: the promise of Hebron
decisions.reason: Caleb had gone through the land as far as Hebron (13:22). Joshua 14:6-14 tells how he received it for his family, as Moses promised. Joshua is named with Caleb in verses 30 and 38.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "slave" for this word, as the style of this translation does; Balanced and Readable say "servant", since the point is belonging to God and serving him, not modern slavery.

decisions.choice: a different attitude
decisions.reason: Readable says what "another spirit" means; it is not God's Spirit here but Caleb's own spirit.

decisions.choice: "ana moyo tofauti" (he has a different heart)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "another spirit" means, as the English "a different attitude" does. In Swahili "moyo" is the everyday word for a person's inner disposition, and it avoids "roho", which readers may take as God's Spirit.

decisions.choice: the Amalekites and Canaanites live in the valley: the reason Israel must turn back now
decisions.reason: The clause explains the command that follows: the way ahead is held by these peoples, and without the LORD Israel cannot go that way. The "valley" is probably the lower land between the wilderness and the hill country. In 13:29 the Amalekites live in the Negev and the Canaanites by the sea and the Jordan; in verses 43-45 both peoples meet Israel in the hill country.

decisions.choice: the way of the Sea of Reeds: the road toward the gulf to the southeast
decisions.reason: The name is the one used for the sea of the crossing (Exodus 13:18; 15:4), known as the Red Sea. Here it most likely means the road toward the gulf east of Sinai, by Ezion-geber (Deuteronomy 1:40; 2:1; 1 Kings 9:26). Israel is sent back the way it came, away from the land.

decisions.choice: turn and set out: the journey into the land is reversed
decisions.reason: Israel had come to the edge of the land (13:26). Now the LORD sends them back into the wilderness, where the generation that refused will die (verses 29-35). Deuteronomy 1:40 recalls the command.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: As in Exodus, Literal says "Sea of Reeds", the meaning of the name, and Balanced and Readable "the Red Sea", the name English readers know.

decisions.choice: the Amalekites and the Canaanites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the singular for each people ("the Amalekite"). Balanced and Readable use the plural, as English does.

en.R: "How long must I put up with this evil community? They keep complaining against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I have heard all the complaints the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} are making against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: how long with this evil congregation: an unfinished question
alternatives: How long will this evil congregation grumble against me?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves out the verb: "How long ... to this evil congregation?" The sense is "How long must I bear with them?" (compare verse 11). Some take the verb from the next clause: "How long will this congregation grumble?" The meaning hardly differs.

decisions.choice: evil: wicked, set against the LORD
decisions.reason: The congregation is called evil because it has turned against the LORD; the same words return in verse 35. The "bad" report of the land in verse 37 is the same word.

decisions.choice: grumbling, grumblings: bitter complaint
decisions.reason: The verb of verse 2 and its noun are repeated three times. The LORD has heard every word, and in verse 28 he takes them at their word.

decisions.choice: [shall I bear] / must I put up with
decisions.reason: Every level supplies the missing verb; Literal shows it in brackets.

decisions.choice: as I live, declares the LORD: a solemn oath
decisions.reason: As in verse 21. "Declares the LORD" (literally "the utterance of the LORD") marks the words as the LORD's own solemn statement.

decisions.choice: as you have spoken in my ears, so I will do: the people get the death they wished for
decisions.reason: The people said, "If only we had died in this wilderness" (verse 2). God takes them at their word: in this wilderness they will die (verse 29). They also said their children would become plunder (verse 3); God answers that too (verse 31).

decisions.choice: surely: the oath word
decisions.reason: The words "if not" in an oath mean "surely": what follows will certainly happen. Compare verse 23, where "if" means "surely not".

decisions.choice: ends with a colon
decisions.reason: What God will do is set out in verses 29-35, so the sentence ends with a colon. The message to the people runs to the end of verse 35.

decisions.choice: "Diles" (singular)
decisions.reason: The speech is to Moses and Aaron, but the Hebrew command "say" is singular, addressed to Moses; Spanish, which must choose, follows the Hebrew. The plural you of the message itself (the people) takes the plural_you setting.

en.L: In this wilderness your corpses will fall, all your enrolled [ones] according to all your number, from twenty years old and upward, who have grumbled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Here in this wilderness your bodies will fall, all of you who were enrolled, the whole number of you from twenty years old and upward, who have grumbled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Your dead bodies will lie in this desert. Every one of you who was counted, everyone twenty years old or older who complained against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, will die.

es.L: En este desierto caerán {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} cadáveres, todos {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} registrados según todo {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} número, de veinte años para arriba, los que {{plural_you:han murmurado|habéis murmurado}} contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

sw.L: Katika nyika hii maiti zenu zitaanguka, wote mliohesabiwa kwa kadiri ya hesabu yenu yote, tangu wenye umri wa miaka ishirini na zaidi, mlioninung'unikia.
